text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish paper this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Finance ministry chief economist Martti Hetemaki says actions against unemployment should be tougher if it is to be halved. He supports bigger differences in income and lower unemployment benefits.
- Draft proposal for a new immigration law transfers asylum interviews to immigration authorities from police.
- Most street names in Helsinki have rural names. The more concrete element buildings there are in an area, the more frequent is nature as a theme for its street names, study shows.

- The only way to effectively remove wrinkles is to peel off the face's skin: the new skin forming becomes tight and soft, Finnish plastic surgeon says. Lotions do not work and face lifts do not really remove wrinkles.

- Finnish-owned Estonian department store Kaubahall risks bankruptcy. Debt estimates vary between 10 and 20 million kroons and some suppliers say they have waited for payments for almost a year. The owners are seeking new financing.
- An increasing amount of trade on the Helsinki stock exchange is between brokerages. Brokerage fees are falling and brokers seek profits in trading, bourse managing director Juhani Erma says.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Tough taxation of concealed dividends which can rise above 100 percent in some cases may force many family companies out of business, professor says.

- Nokia -sponsored Nokia Sugar Bowl was the most watched programme on U.S. television in the week of the turn of the year, with 17.4 million viewers on January 2, survey shows. Nokia says it is very satisfied.
- Some regional cooperative banks say they are prepared to leave the new joint cooperative organisation formed on Wednesday.

- Enso's return paper machine at the Sachsen Papier Eilenburg plant produced more newsprint than any other machine in the world last year, and its Valmet paper machine also broke the speed record with an top output of 1,643 metres per minute, Enso says.
AAMULEHTI
- Ministry of interior considers compulsory fire alarms in tall blocks of flats.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- The average age of children getting diabetes in FInland has fallen to 7-8 years from 10-12 years, but it is not yet known what has caused the change, doctor says.
DEMARI
- Permament under-secretary of state Raimo Sailas says there are chances that the average unemployment rate this year could fall below 15 percent, lower than the official forecast of 15.4 percent.
-- Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 242
